source: An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese (Revised Edition), Chapter 11 単語 list, book pp. 204–206 (PDF pp. 214–216). Covers 会話 1–3 and the 読み物.
notes: Chapter 11's dialogues deal with apologizing, being scolded, and host-family friction; the 読み物 is a 1989 (平成元年) essay by an American exchange student about living with her Japanese host family — blending in, gestures, being scolded, the spirit of independence, and cross-cultural misunderstanding. The deck keeps the words an N3 learner has seen passively but cannot produce (文句, 我慢する, 納得する, 積極的), the chapter's rich 気〜 and 〜込む families, and a handful of N2/N1 stretch words that are common in real descriptive Japanese (みっともない, 相違, 悔やむ, 先手を打つ). Excluded: proper nouns (小川, 真美, ジル, 松本, 平成元年), N4/N5 vocabulary already mastered (問題, 遅い, 喫茶店, 晩ご飯, 手紙, 足, 口, 短い, 明るい, 弟, だめ, 失敗する, 洗濯), transparent collocations (涙を流す, 風邪をひく), and textual conventions (中略, 後略).

priority_guide.high: Learn first — high-frequency word that blocks comprehension if missing.
priority_guide.medium: Learn after high priority — enriches descriptive range; context usually helps.
priority_guide.low: Passive recognition is enough for now — note once, revisit later.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 territory — ambitious but high-frequency in real usage.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading carefully.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Kanji are rare or have irregular readings — learn the kana form first.

cards.context: Almost always appears as 文句を言う (to complain) or 文句がある (to have a complaint). This is everyday grumbling — a formal complaint to a company is 苦情 or クレーム (false friend: クレーム means complaint, never 'claim').
cards.example_sentence: 彼は何を食べても文句を言う。
cards.example_reading: かれ は なに を たべて も もんく を いう。
cards.example_meaning: No matter what he eats, he complains.

cards.simpler_synonym: 謝罪する（しゃざいする）※フォーマル
cards.context: Homophone trap: 誤る (to make a mistake) is also あやまる — context and kanji decide. The person you apologize to takes に: 友達に謝る. The formal noun is 謝罪.
cards.example_sentence: 遅れたことを友達に謝った。
cards.example_reading: おくれた こと を ともだち に あやまった。
cards.example_meaning: I apologized to my friend for being late.

cards.context: Mimetic adverb, nearly always with 会う／出会う for surprise encounters. Secondary sense: collapsing suddenly (ばったり倒れる) or something stopping dead (客足がばったり止まる).
cards.example_sentence: 駅で昔の友達にばったり会った。
cards.example_reading: えき で むかし の ともだち に ばったり あった。
cards.example_meaning: I ran into an old friend at the station.

cards.context: The 〜込む suffix on a verb stem means 'deeply / into': 考え込む (be lost in thought), 溶け込む (blend in), 座り込む (sit down and stay). 話し込む implies losing track of time — exactly why the speaker in 会話1 was late.
cards.example_sentence: 喫茶店で友達と話し込んで、時間を忘れてしまった。
cards.example_reading: きっさてん で ともだち と はなしこんで、じかん を わすれて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I got absorbed talking with a friend at a coffee shop and completely lost track of time.

cards.simpler_synonym: 失望する（しつぼうする）※フォーマル
cards.context: Describes your own deflation; the cause takes に: 結果にがっかりした. To call something disappointing as a judgment, use 残念だ instead. Don't force an English-style transitive 'X disappointed me' — flip it to Xにがっかりした.
cards.example_sentence: 試合に負けて、みんながっかりした。
cards.example_reading: しあい に まけて、みんな がっかり した。
cards.example_meaning: We lost the match and everyone was disappointed.

cards.simpler_synonym: 心配になる（しんぱいになる）
cards.context: Sort the 気 family once: 〜が気になる (it bothers you — involuntary), 〜を気にする (you actively worry about it), 〜に気をつける (you take care), 〜が気にかかる (written variant of 気になる, also in this chapter). The thing bothering you takes が.
cards.example_sentence: 明日の面接のことが気になって眠れない。
cards.example_reading: あした の めんせつ の こと が き に なって ねむれない。
cards.example_meaning: Tomorrow's interview is weighing on my mind and I can't sleep.

cards.context: Two faces: with an affirmative it means 'at any cost' (どうしても行きたい); with a negative it means 'no matter how hard one tries, it won't work' (どうしても覚えられない) — the chapter's grammar note sense.
cards.example_sentence: この漢字だけはどうしても覚えられない。
cards.example_reading: この かんじ だけ は どうしても おぼえられない。
cards.example_meaning: This one kanji I simply cannot memorize, no matter what.

cards.context: 経つ takes only time expressions as its subject. The kanji 経 reads けい in 経験・経済 but たつ here — the textbook often writes it in kana (たつ). Common pattern: 〜ているうちに時間が経つ.
cards.example_sentence: 友達と話していると、時間が経つのを忘れる。
cards.example_reading: ともだち と はなして いる と、じかん が たつ の を わすれる。
cards.example_meaning: When I'm talking with friends, I forget the passing of time.

cards.simpler_synonym: 仲（なか）※人間どうしの親しさ
cards.context: Broad workhorse: 人間関係 (human relations), 〜と関係がある (is connected to), 〜に関係なく (regardless of). For how well two people get along, use 仲がいい／悪い — not 関係がいい.
cards.example_sentence: 日本の会社では人間関係がとても大切だ。
cards.example_reading: にほん の かいしゃ で は にんげんかんけい が とても たいせつ だ。
cards.example_meaning: In Japanese companies, human relationships are extremely important.

cards.context: The chapter uses 独立した (independent) and 独立精神 (spirit of independence) — the value the essay's author feels her host family lacks toward children. 自立 is personal self-reliance; 独立 also covers countries and businesses becoming independent.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は大学を出てすぐ、親から独立した。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は だいがく を でて すぐ、おや から どくりつ した。
cards.example_meaning: She became independent from her parents right after finishing university.

cards.context: For feelings you can't pin down: 何だか悲しい (I feel sad somehow). 何となく is the close cousin — 何だか leans slightly more emotional and conversational. Hugely common in speech; using it makes your Japanese sound natural fast.
cards.example_sentence: 今日は何だか元気が出ない。
cards.example_reading: きょう は なんだか げんき が でない。
cards.example_meaning: For some reason I just have no energy today.

cards.simpler_synonym: 朝寝坊する（あさねぼうする）
cards.context: 朝寝坊 is both the act and the person ('a late riser'). Don't confuse with 昼寝 (a nap, deliberate). In 会話3 the homestay student gets scolded for it — a classic host-family flashpoint.
cards.example_sentence: 寝坊して、授業に三十分も遅れてしまった。
cards.example_reading: ねぼう して、じゅぎょう に さんじゅっぷん も おくれて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I overslept and ended up a whole thirty minutes late to class.

cards.context: 叱る is corrective scolding from a position of responsibility (parent, teacher, boss); 怒る is the emotion of anger, though colloquially it also means 'scold angrily' — the textbook lists おこる that way. You'll meet it most as the passive: 先生に叱られた. Often written in kana (しかる).
cards.example_sentence: 弟は宿題をしなくて、母に叱られた。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は しゅくだい を しなくて、はは に しかられた。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother didn't do his homework and got scolded by our mother.

cards.simpler_synonym: 恥ずかしい（はずかしい）
cards.context: Judges behavior or appearance by how it looks to others — society's eyes, not your inner embarrassment (that's 恥ずかしい). A parent's scolding word: みっともないからやめなさい. Historically from 見とうもない 'not fit to be seen'.
cards.example_sentence: 人の前で大声でけんかするのはみっともない。
cards.example_reading: ひと の まえ で おおごえ で けんか する の は みっともない。
cards.example_meaning: Having a shouting match in front of other people is disgraceful.

cards.simpler_synonym: 話に割り込む（わりこむ）
cards.context: Literally 'insert one's mouth' — wedging yourself into someone else's conversation, usually unwelcome: 人の話に口をはさむ. Part of the chapter's 口 idiom set alongside 口やかましい and 悪口.
cards.example_sentence: 人の話に口をはさむのは失礼だと言われた。
cards.example_reading: ひと の はなし に くち を はさむ の は しつれい だ と いわれた。
cards.example_meaning: I was told that butting into other people's conversations is rude.

cards.context: Like うるさい, it spans 'noisy' and 'nagging': 時間にやかましい (strict about time). The reading also uses 口やかましい (nagging, sharp-tongued) — the essay author's view of her host mother. Slightly more old-fashioned/written than うるさい.
cards.example_sentence: 父は時間にやかましい人だった。
cards.example_reading: ちち は じかん に やかましい ひと だった。
cards.example_meaning: My father was a man who was strict about punctuality.

cards.simpler_synonym: 耐える（たえる）※フォーマル
cards.context: Culturally loaded: silently enduring discomfort is virtue-coded in Japan, and the homestay conflict in this chapter turns on it. Key forms: 我慢できない (can't stand it), 我慢の限界 (the limit of one's patience).
cards.example_sentence: 言いたいことがあっても、我慢して何も言わなかった。
cards.example_reading: いいたい こと が あって も、がまん して なに も いわなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Even though I had things I wanted to say, I held back and said nothing.

cards.simpler_synonym: 生活する（せいかつする）
cards.context: 住む is residing at an address (point-like, takes に); 暮らす is the texture of daily life (一人で暮らす, 幸せに暮らす). The noun is 暮らし (living, livelihood). The essay opens with the author having lived (暮らした) with a Japanese family.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は一年間、日本の家族と一緒に暮らした。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は いちねんかん、にほん の かぞく と いっしょ に くらした。
cards.example_meaning: She lived together with a Japanese family for one year.

cards.context: Prefix directly before numbers: 約三時間 (about three hours). More written/formal than だいたい — use it in essays and reports. Same kanji carries the 'binding' sense in 約束 and 予約; here it's the 'rounded number' sense.
cards.example_sentence: 駅から大学まで約二十分かかる。
cards.example_reading: えき から だいがく まで やく にじゅっぷん かかる。
cards.example_meaning: It takes about twenty minutes from the station to the university.

cards.context: Transitive/intransitive pair: 過ごす is transitive (you spend time, takes を — 楽しい時間を過ごす); 過ぎる is intransitive (time passes by itself — 時間が過ぎる). English 'spend' only maps to 過ごす, never 過ぎる.
cards.example_sentence: 週末は家族とゆっくり過ごした。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ は かぞく と ゆっくり すごした。
cards.example_meaning: I spent the weekend relaxing with my family.

cards.simpler_synonym: 手に入れる（てにいれる）
cards.context: Written/formal verb whose objects are usually abstract: 知識を得る, 経験を得る, 信頼を得る. Also lives on as the suffix 〜得る (ありえる／ありうる 'can possibly be') — both readings survive for the suffix.
cards.example_sentence: 留学で、お金では買えない経験を得た。
cards.example_reading: りゅうがく で、おかね で は かえない けいけん を えた。
cards.example_meaning: Through studying abroad, I gained experience that money can't buy.

cards.context: Irregular reading — えがお, not しょうがお. Japanese doesn't lexically split 'laugh' and 'smile' (笑う covers both), so 笑顔 is how you point specifically at a smile. Collocations: 笑顔を見せる, 笑顔で挨拶する.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女はいつも笑顔で挨拶してくれる。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は いつも えがお で あいさつ して くれる。
cards.example_meaning: She always greets me with a smile.

cards.context: The thing suits the person: 人に〜が似合う — その帽子、よく似合うね is the everyday compliment. Don't confuse with 似ている (to resemble) or 〜と合う (two things go well together). In the essay, a smile 'suits' the host sister.
cards.example_sentence: その着物は彼女によく似合っていた。
cards.example_reading: その きもの は かのじょ に よく にあって いた。
cards.example_meaning: That kimono really suited her.

cards.context: The compact written form of 気を遣う. In speech you'll mostly hear the noun in polite set phrases: お気遣いありがとうございます (thank you for your consideration). Note the rendaku: 遣う reads づかう here.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はいつも周りの人を気遣っている。
cards.example_reading: かれ は いつも まわり の ひと を きづかって いる。
cards.example_meaning: He is always considerate of the people around him.

cards.context: Literally 'melt into' — sugar dissolves into coffee, and a newcomer 溶け込む into a class, team, or culture. The central image of the essay: becoming part of the host family. Same 〜込む family as 話し込む.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女はすぐに新しいクラスに溶け込んだ。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は すぐ に あたらしい クラス に とけこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: She blended into her new class right away.

cards.context: Lives almost entirely in the set phrase 身振り手振りで — 'with gestures and hand motions' — which is exactly how the essay's author communicated before her Japanese improved. 振り is the 'manner of moving' suffix (口振り, 素振り).
cards.example_sentence: 言葉が通じなくて、身振り手振りで説明した。
cards.example_reading: ことば が つうじなくて、みぶり てぶり で せつめい した。
cards.example_meaning: We couldn't understand each other's language, so I explained with gestures.

cards.context: Formal/written word for 違い — at home in essays (文化の相違, 意見の相違) and contracts (相違ありません 'this is correct'). In conversation, stick with 違い; reaching for 相違 in speech sounds stiff.
cards.example_sentence: 二つの国の習慣には大きな相違がある。
cards.example_reading: ふたつ の くに の しゅうかん に は おおきな そうい が ある。
cards.example_meaning: There are major differences between the customs of the two countries.

cards.context: The personality word teachers and bosses use constantly. 積極的に＋verb = doing something of your own initiative (積極的に参加する). Antonym: 消極的 (passive, reserved) — learn them as a pair.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は授業で積極的に質問する。
cards.example_reading: かれ は じゅぎょう で せっきょくてき に しつもん する。
cards.example_meaning: He actively asks questions in class.

cards.simpler_synonym: 質問する（しつもんする）／聞く
cards.context: Homophone trap: 訪ねる (to visit) is also たずねる — only the kanji separates them. 尋ねる is politer and more written than 聞く; the textbook glosses it as ＝質問する.
cards.example_sentence: 駅への道を近くの人に尋ねた。
cards.example_reading: えき へ の みち を ちかく の ひと に たずねた。
cards.example_meaning: I asked a person nearby for the way to the station.

cards.context: The written-register いつも — the textbook flags it as a written expression. Use it in essays, presentations, and formal statements; in casual speech it sounds stiff. Common pattern: 常に〜ようにしている (I make it a rule to always…).
cards.example_sentence: 母は常に家族のことを考えている。
cards.example_reading: はは は つねに かぞく の こと を かんがえて いる。
cards.example_meaning: My mother is always thinking of the family.

cards.context: Intransitive — the thing comes back on its own; the transitive partner is 返す (you return something). Three-way homophone with 帰る (a person goes home) and 変える (to change) — kanji choice is load-bearing. The textbook marks it v.i.
cards.example_sentence: 貸した本がやっと返ってきた。
cards.example_reading: かした ほん が やっと かえって きた。
cards.example_meaning: The book I lent out finally came back.

cards.context: Stronger than 分かる — it means the explanation clicked and you accept it. The negative is essential for disagreements: 納得がいかない／納得できない (I can't accept that). Watch the doubled っ: なっとく.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の説明を聞いて、やっと納得した。
cards.example_reading: かれ の せつめい を きいて、やっと なっとく した。
cards.example_meaning: After hearing his explanation, I was finally convinced.

cards.simpler_synonym: 違う文化（ちがうぶんか）
cards.context: The prefix 異〜 means 'different/other' (異国 foreign land, 異常 abnormal). The reading extends it to 異文化圏 — 〜圏 is the 'sphere' suffix you'll keep meeting: 英語圏 (English-speaking world), 首都圏 (greater Tokyo).
cards.example_sentence: 留学して初めて、異文化の難しさを知った。
cards.example_reading: りゅうがく して はじめて、いぶんか の むずかしさ を しった。
cards.example_meaning: Only after studying abroad did I learn how hard a different culture can be.

cards.context: Formal word — everyday conversation overwhelmingly uses アドバイス. 助言する = to advise. Mind the reading: じょげん, not じょごん. In the essay the host parents' constant 助言 reads as nagging to the American author.
cards.example_sentence: 先生の助言のおかげで、いいレポートが書けた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい の じょげん の おかげ で、いい レポート が かけた。
cards.example_meaning: Thanks to my teacher's advice, I was able to write a good report.

cards.simpler_synonym: 本人がいないところで
cards.context: 陰 is shade/shadow. 陰で悪口を言う = badmouth someone behind their back; the noun 陰口 (かげぐち) means exactly that. Not always negative: 陰で支える is supporting someone from behind the scenes — and おかげで grew from the same root.
cards.example_sentence: 陰で文句を言うより、直接話した方がいい。
cards.example_reading: かげ で もんく を いう より、ちょくせつ はなした ほう が いい。
cards.example_meaning: Rather than complaining behind someone's back, it's better to talk to them directly.

cards.context: Both わるくち and わるぐち are accepted readings. Pairs naturally with 陰で and こそこそと (in whispers) — the essay strings all three together. The opposite act is ほめる (to praise).
cards.example_sentence: 友達の悪口を言うつもりはなかった。
cards.example_reading: ともだち の わるくち を いう つもり は なかった。
cards.example_meaning: I didn't mean to speak ill of my friend.

cards.simpler_synonym: 厳しくない（きびしくない）
cards.context: You know 'sweet' — the figurative senses are the trap: 子供に甘い (soft on the kids, the chapter's 甘くする 'to be lenient'), 考えが甘い (naive thinking), 甘く見る (to underestimate). Antonym in all these: 厳しい.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父は孫にとても甘い。
cards.example_reading: そふ は まご に とても あまい。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather is very soft on his grandchildren.

cards.simpler_synonym: 後悔する（こうかいする）
cards.context: 後悔する is the everyday verb; 悔やむ is more written and more emotional. Same kanji gives you 悔しい (くやしい) — 'frustrating, mortifying' — one of the highest-frequency emotion words in real spoken Japanese.
cards.example_sentence: 今さら悔やんでも、失敗はもう変えられない。
cards.example_reading: いまさら くやんで も、しっぱい は もう かえられない。
cards.example_meaning: Regretting it now won't change the failure.

cards.context: Set pattern: 〜の妨げになる (to get in the way of) — in the essay, parental interference is a 妨げ to children's independence. The verb is 妨げる. Everyday speech prefers 邪魔（になる）; 妨げ is essay register.
cards.example_sentence: 騒音は勉強の妨げになる。
cards.example_reading: そうおん は べんきょう の さまたげ に なる。
cards.example_meaning: Noise gets in the way of studying.

cards.simpler_synonym: 絶対に〜ない（ぜったいに）
cards.context: Must close with a negative — 決して忘れません, never 決して忘れます. Firm, written-leaning tone. Compare 全く〜ない (not at all — degree, also in this chapter) and casual 絶対〜ない. Watch the doubled っ: けっして.
cards.example_sentence: あの日のことは決して忘れない。
cards.example_reading: あの ひ の こと は けっして わすれない。
cards.example_meaning: I will never forget that day.

cards.simpler_synonym: 役に立たない（やくにたたない）
cards.context: Noun and な-adjective: 無駄な時間 (wasted time), 時間の無駄 (a waste of time), 無駄にする (to let go to waste), 無駄遣い (wasting money). 〜ても無駄だ ('no use doing…') is the everyday workhorse pattern.
cards.example_sentence: 心配しても無駄だと分かっていた。
cards.example_reading: しんぱい して も むだ だ と わかって いた。
cards.example_meaning: I knew that worrying would do no good.

cards.context: Written-register 毎日: 日々の生活 (everyday life), 日々努力する (strive daily). The 々 mark repeats the previous kanji with rendaku: ひ＋び. Common in essays and reflective writing — like the essay's closing lines about her days in Japan.
cards.example_sentence: 日本で過ごした日々は今でも忘れられない。
cards.example_reading: にほん で すごした ひび は いま でも わすれられない。
cards.example_meaning: Even now I can't forget the days I spent in Japan.

cards.context: What you felt about an experience — teachers ask 感想を聞かせてください after every activity. 感想文 is the school reaction essay; the chapter's reading comes from a 感想文集 (collection of student essays). Distinct from 意見 (a position you argue).
cards.example_sentence: 映画を見た感想を友達と話し合った。
cards.example_reading: えいが を みた かんそう を ともだち と はなしあった。
cards.example_meaning: I talked over my impressions of the movie with a friend.

meanings: to act before the other person
cards.simpler_synonym: 先にやっておく（さきに）
cards.context: From board games — playing the first stone (先手 = first move, 打つ = to play/strike). Acting in anticipation of the other person's move: in the essay, apologizing before the host mother can scold. Opposite: 後手に回る (to be stuck reacting).
cards.example_sentence: 怒られる前に、先手を打って謝った。
cards.example_reading: おこられる まえ に、せんて を うって あやまった。
cards.example_meaning: Before I could get told off, I made the first move and apologized.

cards.context: Suffix on Sino-Japanese nouns: 教育上 (for educational reasons — the essay's usage), 健康上, 仕事上, 規則上. Written/formal register. Read じょう, never うえ, in this use; often followed by の＋noun or a clause.
